key_insight: UniTB combines physical priors with equivariant deep learning to predict electronic Hamiltonians across diverse chemistries while constraining unphysical band shifts.
engineering_relevance: Its fast Hamiltonian predictions support large-cell electronic-property calculations and materials screening, with UniTB-Flash offering linear-cost prior assembly.
method: Learn corrections to a density-functional tight-binding prior using an E(3)-equivariant network.
Use prior-routed mixture-of-experts learning and a charge-equilibration head to generalize across chemistry.
Bound band shifts through projection; accelerate computation with SO(2) GPU kernels and two-center tables in UniTB-Flash.
evidence_signal: Trained on 29,242 crystals, UniTB achieves 0.48 meV matrix-element error on nonmagnetic test crystals spanning 68 elements; both variants reproduce DFT optics and conductivity for amorphous Ge-Sb-Te without amorphous training data.
watch_item: UniTB-Flash preserves candidate rankings in the reported evaluation but yields less accurate property values than UniTB.
paper_title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning
